messages:
Emma Chen: anyone seen this before? CI started failing decrypt after we rotated the CMK. error from aws cli: 
```
An error occurred (AccessDeniedException) when calling the Decrypt operation: User: arn:aws:sts::111111111:assumed-role/ci-deploy-role/session is not authorized to perform: kms:Decrypt on resource arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:222222222:key/abcd-ef01-2345
```
Rahul Patel: quick q — is the CMK in the same account as the role? and are you using grants or key policy to allow it?
Emma Chen: same account. we use envelope encryption: S3 obj encrypted with a data key generated by that CMK. No explicit grant that I know of, just key policy + role IAM policy. started right after we rotated keys yesterday.
Lina Gomez: check two things: (1) key policy principal includes the role (not just the root account) and (2) the role's IAM policy allows kms:Decrypt. simple miss is key policy was left only allowing the previous role ARN.
Rahul Patel: also watch for conditions on encryption context. If the CMK policy used `kms:EncryptionContext:$contextKey` conditions then Decrypt will deny if the call doesn't pass the same context.
Emma Chen: how to test quickly from my laptop as the assumed role? should I aws sts assume-role then run aws kms decrypt?
Mike Ruiz: yes. do `aws sts assume-role --role-arn arn:aws:iam::111111111:role/ci-deploy-role --role-session-name test` then export creds and run `aws kms decrypt --ciphertext-blob fileb://blob --key-id arn:aws:kms:... --query Plaintext --output text | base64 --decode`.
Emma Chen: ran that. same AccessDenied.
Rahul Patel: post key policy snippet (sanitize ARNs). common gotcha: key policy might be allowing `arn:aws:iam::111111111:root` but not the role principal; assumed-role ARNs are `arn:aws:sts::...:assumed-role/...`. KMS key policy must list the IAM role ARN (the role resource `arn:aws:iam::111111111:role/ci-deploy-role`) or the account root. Example allow block we use:
```
{
  "Effect": "Allow",
  "Principal": {"AWS": "arn:aws:iam::111111111:role/ci-deploy-role"},
  "Action": ["kms:Decrypt","kms:GenerateDataKey"],
  "Resource": "*"
}
```
Lina Gomez: if you used `aws:PrincipalArn` condition on the key policy, it must match the `sts:assumed-role/*` pattern for the session. That can bite if you put a different pattern.
Mike Ruiz: another angle: any KMS grants in play? if you created a grant for the old role and rotated CMK, grant tokens might be needed. Grants are tied to grantee principal; if grant existed for old role ARN and you recreated the role or name changed, it won't apply.
Emma Chen: no grants in the account for that CMK.
Rahul Patel: check Service Control Policies (SCPs) or IAM permission boundaries — an explicit deny can override. Also look at CloudTrail event for kms:Decrypt to see which principal was evaluated.
Emma Chen: grabbing cloudtrail now... shows principal arn:aws:sts::111111111:assumed-role/ci-deploy-role:session-abc. Condition shows `kms:EncryptionContext:purpose: deploy` present on the Encrypt call earlier. Hmm maybe CI isn't attaching same context on decrypt.
Lina Gomez: yep that's it — encrypt called with EncryptionContext {"purpose":"deploy"}. KMS enforces exact match when the key policy requires it. Quick fix: either stop requiring the context in key policy, or ensure the decrypt caller passes `--encryption-context`.
Mike Ruiz: example cli decrypt with context: `aws kms decrypt --ciphertext-blob fileb://blob --encryption-context purpose=deploy --key-id arn:aws:kms:...`.
Emma Chen: tried adding the context and decrypt succeeded locally.
Rahul Patel: for the CI pipeline, add the encryption context key/value into the decrypt step or remove context condition if it's not providing security value.
Emma Chen: put a small change in the pipeline to pass `ENCRYPTION_CONTEXT=purpose=deploy` to the aws cli. re-run CI now.
ops-bot: deploy-pipeline #1234 started by Emma Chen
Emma Chen: ✅ CI passed now. thanks all. follow-ups: we should document that rotation needs update to pipeline (data key generation vs decrypt flags) and add a unit test simulating encrypt/decrypt with ctx.
Lina Gomez: and maybe add a rubric in runbook: "If AccessDenied on Decrypt after rotation -> check key policy principals, encryption context, grants, SCPs".
Mike Ruiz: I'll open a short RFC to add the test and a template pipeline snippet.
Emma Chen: nice, closing this thread. :tada:
